A.explanation: Uses the change in speed $5.0 - 4.0 = 1.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ instead of the total velocity reversal from $-5.0$ to $+4.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

B.explanation: This is the momentum change of one pellet, $0.00060 \times 9.0 = 0.0054 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$, without multiplying by the pellet rate per second.

C.explanation: Equals the rate of change of momentum: $0.00060 \times 9.0 \times 100/60 = 0.0090 \text{ N}$.

D.explanation: Uses 100 pellets per minute as 100 per second, omitting division by 60, giving $100 \times 0.0054 = 0.54 \text{ N}$.

hints: Notice the pellets reverse direction, so take downward as negative and upward as positive when finding the velocity change from $5.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ down to $4.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ up.
Recall that average force equals rate of change of momentum, so you need the momentum change of one $0.60 \text{ g}$ pellet and the number of pellets per second from 100 per minute.
Convert $0.60 \text{ g}$ to $\text{kg}$ and 100 per minute to per second, then multiply the per-pellet $m\Delta v$ by that rate to get force in $\text{N}$.
walkthrough: Convert given quantities to SI units: $m = 0.60 \text{ g} = 0.00060 \text{ kg}$ and pellet rate $N = 100/60 = 1.67 \text{ s}^{-1}$.
Choose a sign convention, for example up positive. Then initial velocity $u = -5.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and final velocity $v = +4.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Change in momentum of one pellet is $\Delta p = m(v-u) = 0.00060 \times [4.0 - (-5.0)] = 0.00060 \times 9.0 = 0.0054 \text{ kg m s}^{-1}$.
Average force on the pellets equals total momentum change per second: $F = N\Delta p = (100/60) \times 0.0054$.
Calculate $F = 1.67 \times 0.0054 = 0.0090 \text{ N}$. By Newton's third law this is also the average force on the plate. This is option C.
